title: Exact sections identify principal derived reduction with the actual scalar-extension unit
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site with final object $U$, and suppose $\Gamma=\Gamma(U,-)$ is exact on abelian sheaves. Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $t\in R$ such that multiplication by $t$ on $R$ is injective. Put $A=R/(t)$ with its specified quotient map. Let $\mathcal O\to\mathcal O'$ be a surjection of sheaves of commutative rings and let $R\to\Gamma(\mathcal O)$, $A\to\Gamma(\mathcal O')$ be compatible coefficient maps. Assume $0\to\mathcal O\xrightarrow{t}\mathcal O\to\mathcal O'\to0$ is exact, with $\mathcal O'=\mathcal O/t\mathcal O$. Use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], their derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and exact coefficient restriction [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. Let $G:D(\mathcal O)\to D(R)$ and $G':D(\mathcal O')\to D(A)$ be exact sections with these scalar restrictions. Write $T=-\otimes^L_{\mathcal O}\mathcal O'$ and $L=-\otimes_R^LA$ with the normalized extension/restriction adjunctions [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction]. For every $N\in D(\mathcal O)$ there is a natural isomorphism $\alpha_N:LGN\xrightarrow{\sim}G'TN$ satisfying
$$\operatorname{Res}_{R\to A}(\alpha_N)\circ u_{GN}=G(v_N),$$
where $u$ and $v$ are the ordinary-module and sheaf derived scalar-extension units and exact sections identify the two restricted targets. This specifies $\alpha_N$ uniquely as the scalar-extension adjunct of $G(v_N)$. Its normalization on any flat-term K-flat sheaf resolution $P\to N$ [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules] is $\theta_P\circ c_{\Gamma P}$ as defined in [lem-pod-derived-reduction-sheaf-resolution-independence]: $\theta_P$ sends a section modulo $t$ to its quotient section. On any flat-term K-flat ordinary-module resolution $q:Q\to\Gamma P$, the resulting representative is $Q/tQ\to\Gamma(P/tP)$, $\bar x\mapsto q(x)\bmod t$, and its adjunct is $Q\to\Gamma(P/tP)$, $x\mapsto q(x)\bmod t$. These formulas are independent of both resolutions; no K-flatness of $\Gamma P$ is assumed.

proof.text: The underlying abelian sheaf is unchanged by coefficient restriction. Thus, for an $\mathcal O'$-complex $H$, $\operatorname{Res}_{R\to A}G'H=G\operatorname{Res}_{\mathcal O\to\mathcal O'}H$, with the scalar actions equal by the assumed coefficient square. Exactness of sections gives $H^j(\Gamma K)=\Gamma H^j(K)$: compute cycles as kernels and cohomology as cokernels of boundaries into cycles. Consequently sections preserve quasi-isomorphisms and induce $G,G'$ on the localized categories. These identifications also apply to maps, not only objects.

source.place: Tag 03DA, lemma-abelian; elementary consequence of the assumed exactness of sections and derived.tex Tag 05RU, definition-derived-category.

proof.text:
Represent $N$ by a complex $M$ and choose a quasi-isomorphism $p:P\to M$ with $P$ K-flat and flat terms, using the sheaf resolution theorem. Tensoring the assumed coefficient exact sequence with $P^j$ stays exact by the definition of flatness. In particular $t:P^j\to P^j$ is a monomorphism, so $t:C^j\to C^j$ is injective for $C=\Gamma P$. Use the comparison supplied by the resolution-independence node:
$$\beta_P=\theta_Pc_C: L(Q_RC)\longrightarrow G'T(Q_{\mathcal O}P).$$
Its $\theta_P:C/tC\cong\Gamma(P/tP)$ sends the class of a section to its quotient section; its naturality in $P$ and its independence under transport along $p$ are precisely the assertions of that node. The hypotheses hold with the specified quotient $R\to A=R/(t)$ and its specified compatible coefficient map; no assumption that $R$ is a domain is needed.

proof.text:
Choose a flat-term K-flat ordinary-module resolution $q:Q\to C$. The ordinary resolution theorem supplies it without boundedness. Tensoring the injection $t:R\to R$ with each flat module $Q^j$ preserves injectivity, by flat tensor exactness, so multiplication by $t$ is injective on every $Q^j$. Write $\bar q:Q/tQ\to C/tC$. Specialize mixed derived tensor to $A[0]$, identifying ordinary tensor with quotient by $x\otimes\bar a\mapsto ax\bmod t$ and inverse $\bar x\mapsto x\otimes1$. Its natural counit gives
$$c_C\,L(Q_Rq)=Q_A(\bar q)c_Q.$$
Here $c_Q:L(Q_RQ)\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_A(Q/tQ)$ is invertible by K-flatness. Hence, after identifying $L(Q_RC)$ with $Q_A(Q/tQ)$ through $q$, the map $\beta_P$ is represented by $\theta_P\bar q$, namely $\bar x\mapsto q(x)\bmod t$. This derives the representative from the actual universal counit; it does not assume $C$ K-flat.

source.place: Tag 06Y4, lemma-K-flat-resolution; Tag 06Y6, lemma-derived-base-change and its preceding construction; algebra.tex Tag 00HD, lemma-flat.

proof.text: The map $q:Q\to C$ is a quasi-isomorphism and both complexes have termwise injective multiplication by $t$, by steps 2 and 3. Apply the existing principal-quotient quasi-isomorphism theorem to the specified surjection $R\to A$, whose kernel is $tR$. It says exactly that $\bar q:Q/tQ\to C/tC$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Thus $Q_A(\bar q)$ is invertible. The formula in step 3 shows $c_C$ invertible because $c_Q$ and $L(Q_Rq)$ are invertible. Since $\theta_P$ is already an isomorphism, $\beta_P$ is an isomorphism. This argument works in $D(A)$ itself and uses regularity of $t$ on $R$ only to establish regularity on the flat terms of $Q$.

source.place: Tag 06YY, lemma-derived-base-change: principal-quotient comparison; the existing principal-quotient quasi-isomorphism lemma supplies the quotient step. Localization at quasi-isomorphisms is derived.tex Tag 05RU, definition-derived-category.

proof.text:
We now check the unit, including its normalization. Apply the normalized sheaf coefficient adjunction both on $\mathcal C$ and on the one-object site with only the identity cover. Modules on the latter site are literally ordinary modules; its tensor, restriction and derived extension are the ordinary ones. On that site the derived extension $-\otimes^{\mathbf L}_RA$ of [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] and the mixed derived tensor of [lem-pc-mixed-tensor-pointwise-left-derived] with second factor $A[0]$ are both left derived functors of $E\mapsto E\otimes_RA$ with respect to quasi-isomorphisms; by the universal property of left derived functors there is a unique isomorphism between them compatible with their structure maps. Both structure maps are invertible at the flat-term K-flat complex $Q$, so this isomorphism carries the canonical isomorphism $c_Q$ of the adjunction statement to the counit $c_Q$ of step 3; we identify the two throughout. For $P$, the sheaf unit $v$ is represented by $\pi_P:P\to P/tP$. For the flat-term K-flat ordinary complex $Q$, the module unit satisfies $\operatorname{Res}(c_Q)u_{Q_RQ}=Q_R(\pi_Q)$. Naturality of $u$ for $Q_Rq$ and the counit equation from step 3 give
$$\operatorname{Res}(\beta_P)u_{Q_RC}Q_Rq
=Q_R(\theta_P\bar q\pi_Q)
=Q_R(\pi_Cq),$$
where $\pi_C:C\to\Gamma(P/tP)$ is the sectionwise quotient: the second equality sends $x$ on both sides to the quotient section of $q(x)$. Cancel the invertible $Q_Rq$ to obtain $\operatorname{Res}(\beta_P)u_{Q_RC}=G(v_{Q_{\mathcal O}P})$. Equivalently, the adjunct of the representative $\theta_P\bar q$ is $Q\to\Gamma(P/tP)$, $x\mapsto q(x)\bmod t$, by clause (2) of the normalized adjunction.

proof.text: For every choice of the ordinary resolution $q$, step 3 expresses its representative as the same intrinsic map $\theta_Pc_C$, after the canonical K-flat computation of $L(Q_RC)$. Thus changing $q$ changes neither that derived map nor its adjunct. Changing $P\to M$ preserves the transported map by step 6, and the unit equation characterizes its adjunct without any resolution choice. These observations prove both requested independence assertions and all the representative formulas in the statement. At no point was K-flatness or flatness of $\Gamma P$ inferred.

Step 4: principal-quotient-quasi-iso needs no domain hypothesis, so c_C and β_P are invertible. I recomputed the step 5 identity Res(β_P)u_C Q(q) = Q(π_C q) and the step 6 identity Res(α_N)u_{GN} = G(v_N); uniqueness and naturality follow from the adjunction bijection. Edge cases checked: point site with Z, t=2, N=Z/2[0]; t a unit; Z×Z with t=(2,3), where the domain-only nodes could not be cited.
